content: Sva vishaya asamprayoge chittasya svarupanukara ivendriyanam pratyaharah. (Sensory withdrawal is when the senses disengage from external objects and rest in the nature of the mind).
author: Patanjali
explanation:
In the profound psychology of the Yoga Sutras, Patanjali outlines the systematic roadmap for stilling mental fluctuations into radiant, sovereign stillness.

This teaching (Sva vishaya asamprayoge chittasya svarupanukara ivendriyanam...) focuses directly on vishaya and asamprayoge. When we clear away reactive illusions and anchor ourselves in timeless principles, the mind recovers its pristine clarity and inner resilience.

True realization is never an abstract intellectual debate—it is an active discipline lived through quiet integrity and conscious presence in everyday moments.
practicalInsight: Apply this teaching on vishaya today: take a deliberate pause before reacting, align your actions with quiet integrity, and refuse to let transient friction disturb your center.
reflectionPrompt: How can you embody deeper vishaya and asamprayoge in the primary challenge you are navigating right now?
